interview.hardest_part: Maintaining enough inspection throughput while accurately checking increasingly complex documents. With the clock running during reasoning and only one click or drag per turn, each traveler can consume substantial in-game time. Reaching day 29 and a qualifying ending within three hours is a major additional constraint.
interview.likely_failure: An early-to-midgame financial collapse: processing too few travelers to cover household expenses, compounded by citations from missed discrepancies. Even if I remain solvent, I may exhaust the wall-clock budget before the late-game milestones.
interview.helpful_mechanics: Repeatable document layouts and explicit daily rules support a consistent inspection routine. Early inspections are relatively simple, the first two citations each day generally carry no monetary penalty, and milestone credit persists once earned. A loyal-government route can avoid the extra tasks and risks involved in engineering an EZIC victory or escape.
interview.harmful_mechanics: The live clock makes deliberation costly, and every document movement, inspection interaction, stamp, and return requires a separate action. Later days add overlapping requirements, small visual details, and exceptions. Low throughput reduces wages while household costs continue, and scripted events or incorrect story decisions can cause endings that do not qualify.
